problem: Annotated real-world 3D scene data is scarce and expensive, while prior internet-video efforts (RoomTour3D, NaVILA) stay in navigation and treat the multi-module data pipeline as a black box, with no analysis of bottlenecks or error propagation.
motivation: Unlike 2D, 3D data has not scaled since ScanNet, yet the internet holds vast unlabeled room-tour videos. The paper asks whether modular data engines (SfM, depth, segmentation, VLM captioning) can turn them into training data across perception-to-reasoning tasks, and which factors decide whether it helps.
key_idea: Build automated modular data engines that lift unlabeled internet room-tour videos into 3D scenes (poses, meshes, instances, QA, navigation trajectories) and use the data to pretrain or finetune end-to-end models for detection, spatial VQA and VLN.
insight: Generated data helps most for general, domain-agnostic knowledge (relative distance/direction, detection initialization) and less for domain-specific knowledge (object count, room size), where distribution mismatch (KL 1.04 vs 0.145 for counting) dominates. Task-specific processing is essential: in VLN, removing trajectory refinement or instruction enrichment sharply cuts SR (0.228 to 0.177 or 0.074 after R2R finetuning). Models that depend on precomputed segments (Mask3D) are brittle to distribution shift, while models on raw modalities scale more robustly.
method: Video curation: TransNetV2 shot splitting, filtering of humans/outdoor/black frames, parallax-based keyframes, Mast3R-style dense matching plus COLMAP bundle adjustment with pseudo-track pixels, and human quality check (<10 s/scene); 8,217 videos yield 6,687 scenes.
Dense reconstruction: project SfM sparse points into sparse depth maps, feed them as priors to PriorDA for dense metric depth, then TSDF fusion with truncation and outlier filtering (71 s/scene).
Instance segmentation: CropFormer 2D masks lifted to 3D via MaskClustering-style view consensus; Describe Anything and Qwen2-VL give labels mapped to ScanNet categories (96 s/scene).

Spatial VQA generation: build 3D scene graphs (SceneVerse-style) and fill VLM-3R-style templates for 6 question types; Route Planning QA comes from VLM-summarized navigation trajectories with masked turns; 632K QA total, 202K sampled for training.

VLN data generation: path pre-processing (0.5 m clustering, splitting on backtracking, dropping >90° rotations or >70 cm steps), action encoding to R2R discrete actions with Depth-Pro scale calibration, and VLM CoT instruction generation in three styles; 9,631 trajectories.
Downstream training: SpatialLM (3D detection), Mask3D (instance segmentation), Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B with LoRA (VSI-Bench), LLaVA-Video (R2R), evaluated zero-shot, finetuned, and mixed.

setting.backbone: LLaVA-Video (fine-tuned) for VLN; Qwen2.5-VL-3B/7B (LoRA) for VQA; SpatialLM and Mask3D for perception
setting.training_data: Pretraining on generated data from 6,687 internet scenes: 9,631 VLN trajectories (x3 instructions), 632K spatial VQA (202K used), 3D instance annotations; then optional finetuning on R2R / ScanNet
setting.observation: Egocentric RGB video frames for VLN and VQA; 3D point clouds for detection and segmentation
setting.action_space: Discrete R2R-style low-level actions: forward 25/50/75 cm, turn 15/30/45°
setting.simulator: Matterport3D simulator (R2R); ScanNet, ARKitScenes and VSI-Bench for the others

results: Internet-generated data gives strong zero-shot gains: Qwen2.5-VL VSI-Bench +14.9 (3B) and +9.8 (7B), comparable to ScanNet/ScanNet++ GT data on the ARKit subset. Pretraining on it lifts SpatialLM ScanNet F1@.25 from 38.0 to 58.6 and R2R SR from 0.088 (R2R only) to 0.228 after finetuning; Mask3D zero-shot transfer is poor.
limitations: Minimal experimental settings due to compute; small VLN base model and data scale, so no state-of-the-art VLN comparison.
Domain gap and distribution bias (object count, room size, Mask3D segment sensitivity, sim-vs-real visual gap makes naive mixing weak); the pipeline relies on human quality checks.
Static indoor scenes only; privacy concerns with internet videos.
